_note: Plain-language log of notable changes to BetterMati.org, rendered at /changelog. One entry per release, newest first. Start a release with `npm run release` (repo root): it bumps version.json (minor by default; pass patch for fix-only releases) and drafts this entry from the commits since the last release. Rewrite every TODO line for residents before committing; npm test fails while any remain. type is one of new | improved | fixed. Leave out developer-only work (CI, refactors, tests, docs).

changes.text: Separate pages for Elected officials, City offices and Barangays, each with a search filter.
An About page explaining why BetterMati.org exists, how information is checked, and that it is independent of the City Government.
A Site index listing every section of the site, and this changelog.
A Data sources page listing every dataset on the site, who stands behind it, when it was last checked, and how far it is verified.

A Transparency section: City finances for FY2021–FY2025, projects and procurement, 22 archived Full Disclosure reports, an official documents library, and an explanation of how the site publishes data.
Searchable projects and procurement tables, now including the 12 notices the City has open on PhilGEPS, each linked to its official notice.
An Official links page listing the City’s websites, online services and Facebook page, plus the national portals that cover Mati, each checked.
Site-wide search: the search button now looks across every page, service, office, project, procurement notice, document and official link.
Service category and guide pages now have a search box, an at-a-glance summary, and a clear official-source section.
A rewritten accessibility statement that lists what the site does today and its known limitations.
A new footer with links to every main section, and screen readers now announce the page in the language you choose.
The Contact, FAQ, Terms, Privacy, legislation and News pages now match the rest of the site, and the Contact page puts emergency numbers first.
Menus in the top navigation open when you point at them with a mouse.
Pages load faster on phones: each page now downloads only the code it needs instead of the whole site at once.
Opening a new page now starts at the top instead of keeping the previous page's scroll position.
A mistyped or outdated link now shows a proper "Page not found" page instead of an error screen.
The footer's Citizen's Charter link no longer worked on the City website; it is replaced by the official documents library, which lists the Charter as unavailable.
The Sangguniang Panlungsod link in the Site index pointed to a web address that does not exist; it now opens the council’s page on the City website.
The FAQ no longer claims the City is preparing online payments; it says what we actually found.
The whole site was restyled with a cleaner layout, neutral colours and clearer headings.
The emergency hotline strip is easier to read, keeps the numbers on one line, and links to the full hotline list.
The language selector moved into the top bar, and the top bars stay in view as you scroll.
A Visit Mati guide with pages for Dahican Beach, Mount Hamiguitan, Pujada Bay, the Sleeping Dinosaur and the Subangan Museum.
A homepage section highlighting city projects.
Service listings were reorganised and linked to the official documents they are based on.
The site has a proper icon when added to a phone's home screen.
Elected officials now show names verified from the May 2025 local election.
The Statistics and Budget pages were reworked with clearer charts and layout.
A language dropdown in the header for switching between English, Filipino and Cebuano.
The emergency hotline numbers were updated from a sourced list.
The whole site was rebuilt as a faster, pre-rendered app, including all 22 service guides.
Core facts about the City of Mati were corrected across the site.
Reference data for Mati's 26 barangays, based on the PSA's official geographic codes.
The Statistics page now carries City of Mati branding.
The project was rebranded as BetterMati.org for the City of Mati, Davao Oriental.
The first version of the site, built from an open-source local-government portal template.
